question.stem: A delivery drone is flying in a straight line, descending at a constant speed of 12 $\text{m s}^{-1}$ along a path at 20° below the horizontal. It releases a package when the package is 35 m above level ground. Air resistance on the package is negligible unless stated.
question.diagramAlt: A drone moves down and to the right along a dashed straight path at an angle theta below the horizontal. At the moment of release the package has velocity v along the same direction. The height h of the package above the level ground is marked.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Show that the vertical component of the package's velocity at the moment of release is about 4 $\text{m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Determine the time taken for the package to reach the ground.
markscheme: Allow ECF from (a); accept 2.21 to 2.36 s. Award [1 max] for $t = \sqrt{2h/g}$ = 2.67 s (initial velocity ignored).

mistakes.feedback: The package already has a downward velocity when it is released, so it reaches the ground sooner than a package dropped from rest.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Calculate the horizontal distance travelled by the package between release and landing.
markscheme: Allow ECF from (b); accept 24.7 to 26.9 m

mistakes.feedback: Only the horizontal component of the velocity carries the package sideways: use v cos θ, not v.

parts.label: d
parts.question: In practice, air resistance acts on the package. Outline how this affects the horizontal distance travelled by the package before it lands.
markscheme: Air resistance acts opposite to the package's velocity, so it has a horizontal component backwards / the horizontal velocity decreases during the fall ✓
so the package travels a smaller horizontal distance / lands closer to the point below the release point ✓

v.what: speed of the drone (and package) at release

theta.what: angle of the drone's path below the horizontal

h.what: height of the package above the ground at release

parts.label: a
parts.examinerNote: The package has the drone's velocity at release; resolve it. Needs the unrounded value or the working.

parts.label: b
parts.examinerNote: Either solve the quadratic in t, or find the final vertical speed first and use v = u + at. The initial downward velocity must be included.

parts.label: c
parts.examinerNote: Horizontal velocity is constant with no air resistance.

parts.label: d
parts.examinerNote: Qualitative only (the guide limits A.1 calculations to no air resistance). The time of flight also increases slightly, but the decreasing horizontal speed dominates.
